<issue identifier="MM-449">
<title>Wallet: background repo-backup passes via BGProcessingTask</title>
<description>
Extend the wallet's background media-backup scheduling (<issue id="107edb83-8bb7-4fa6-a73b-d336a06dc5f8" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-444/wallet-background-media-backup-passes-via-bgprocessingtask">MM-444</issue>, `BGProcessingTask`) to also drive the repo CAR snapshot, so an opted-in identity's **repo** mirror stays topped up without opening the app — same mechanism, both mirrors refresh together off-foreground. Posts made days ago shouldn't sit un-backed-up until the next launch.

Design plan: `docs/design-plans/2026-07-22-wallet-repo-icloud-backup.md` §Out of scope (branch `claude/wallet-mst-repo-icloud-backup-3qe7wl`, PR #390).

Depends on <issue id="aa55139a-282f-4498-9c12-4a890a3416a9" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-447/wallet-user-held-mst-repo-backup-to-icloud-drive-car-snapshot">MM-447</issue> (the repo backup) and <issue id="107edb83-8bb7-4fa6-a73b-d336a06dc5f8" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-444/wallet-background-media-backup-passes-via-bgprocessingtask">MM-444</issue> (the `BGProcessingTask` plumbing for the blob mirror). Ideally the background task runs both the blob and repo passes for each opted-in identity in one wake-up.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The registered `BGProcessingTask` runs `run_repo_backup(did)` for every repo-backup-opted-in identity, alongside the blob pass, without opening the app.
2. Repo backup opt-in is honored independently of blob backup opt-in (a user can enable one and not the other).
</description>
<team name="Mal's Machinations"/>
<label>Mobile: Identity Wallet</label>
<label>Wave 3: Key Sovereignty</label>
<project name="ezpds">An easy-to-host PDS on the ATProtocol, MacOS. Grandma-approved.</project>

<blocked-by><issue-ref identifier="MM-447" title="Wallet: user-held MST repo backup to iCloud Drive (CAR snapshot)"/></blocked-by>
<related><issue-ref identifier="MM-444" title="Wallet: background media-backup passes via BGProcessingTask"/></related>
</issue-relations>
</issue>

# Linear Development Workflow

This skill manages the full lifecycle of working on a Linear issue: from picking it up through opening a PR.

## Starting Work on an Issue

When the user indicates they want to work on a Linear issue (e.g., "Let's work on MM-42"):

1. **Parse the issue identifier** from the user's message. The pattern is `MM-` followed by a number.

2. **Fetch the issue details** from Linear using the `get_issue` tool with the parsed identifier. Display a brief summary to the user: title, description (truncated if long), priority, and any existing labels.

3. **Update the issue in Linear:**
   - Set the status to **"In Progress"**
   - Assign it to **"me"** (the authenticated user)

   Use the `save_issue` tool with the issue's `id`, `state: "In Progress"`, and `assignee: "me"`.

4. **Create a git branch from a fresh base** using the issue's suggested branch name:
   - The `get_issue` response includes a `branchName` field — use that as the branch name.
   - **Fetch first, then branch from the remote tip — never from a possibly-stale local HEAD:**
     `git fetch origin main && git checkout -b <branchName> origin/main`
     A stale base silently duplicates work that already merged (hours lost rebuilding an already-shipped backend is the known failure mode).
   - If the branch already exists locally, check it out, then run `git log --oneline <branchName>..origin/main` and surface to the user how far behind the base is.

5. **Verify sibling work is in the base.** If the issue depends on or overlaps sibling issues already marked Done in Linear, confirm their PRs are actually present in the branch base (e.g. `git log --oneline origin/main | grep -i mm-nnn`, or check for the files/routes they added) before concluding any related feature is "missing". **"Linear says Done but the code isn't here" is a hard stop-and-verify signal — it almost always means your base is stale, not that the feature needs building.**

6. **Confirm to the user** what happened: issue assigned, status updated, branch created/checked out (and from which base commit). Then ask what they'd like to tackle first, or summarize the issue so they can dive in.

## Opening a PR (Auto-transition to "In Review")

When the user asks to open a PR, create a pull request, or you detect that a PR is being created for a branch associated with a Linear issue:

1. **Identify the Linear issue** from the current branch name. Linear branch names typically contain the issue identifier (e.g., `malpercio/mm-42-fix-the-thing`). Extract the `MM-XXX` portion.

2. **Create the PR** as the user requests (follow normal PR creation workflow).

3. **After the PR is successfully created**, update the Linear issue:
   - Set the status to **"In Review"**
   - Attach the PR URL as a link on the issue using the `links` field in `save_issue`

   Use `save_issue` with the issue's `id`, `state: "In Review"`, and `links: [{"url": "<pr-url>", "title": "Pull Request"}]`.

4. **Confirm** to the user that the issue has been moved to "In Review" and the PR link has been attached.

## Important Notes

- Always fetch the issue first to confirm it exists and get the full `id` (UUID) needed for updates.
- If the issue is already "In Progress" and assigned, skip those updates and just create the branch.
- If branch creation fails (e.g., uncommitted changes), inform the user and suggest next steps rather than silently failing.
- The PR-to-"In Review" transition should happen automatically whenever a PR is opened during a session where the user started work on a Linear issue. Track the active issue identifier throughout the session.

content.content:
1	# Wallet-Held MST Repo Backup to iCloud
2	
3	**Status: core shipped (MM-447, 2026-07-23 — PR #394, in v0.7.2). Follow-ons open;
4	plan retained for them.** This plan proposed — and the wallet now ships — a
5	`repo_backup.rs` module in the identity wallet that mirrors a user's ATProto repo
6	(their signed commit + MST + records — the CAR) into their iCloud Drive, as the
7	sibling of the user-held blob backup (`blob_backup.rs`, MM-434). It closed the last
8	gap in the wallet's self-custody story: until this landed, the repo was the one
9	account asset that lived *only* on the PDS.
10	
11	What shipped under MM-447 (the "Definition of Done" below, minus item 3's migration
12	wiring): the four fine-grained Tauri commands + the `pub(crate) mirror_repo_car`
13	helper, opt-in per DID, the public-`getRepo` fetch with client-side CAR validation
14	before write, the shared iCloud root reused from `blob_backup`, and the "Back up your
15	posts" section folded into the Media Backup screen. What is **not** yet built, tracked
16	as follow-ons (see the sections below): consuming `mirror_repo_car` from the migration
17	`transfer_repo` drain (MM-448); background repo passes via `BGProcessingTask` (MM-449,
18	the repo sibling of the media sweep — repo backup is currently on-demand + opportunistic
19	on app open only, never off-foreground); block-level incremental storage (MM-450,
20	deferred / on ice); and the sovereign disaster-recovery rebuild (MM-451). This file
21	stays in `design-plans/` rather than moving to `archive/` because those follow-ons still
22	reference its design.
23	
24	## Summary
25	
26	The wallet already gives a user three self-controlled copies of the pieces of their
27	identity: the **keys** (device key in the Secure Enclave, recovery Share 1 in the
28	iCloud Keychain), and the **blobs** (media mirrored to iCloud Drive by
29	`blob_backup.rs`). The one asset with no user-held copy is the **repo** — the signed
30	commit + Merkle Search Tree + record blocks that hold every post, like, follow, and
31	profile edit. It lives on the PDS as the primary and only copy
32	(`docs/pds-architecture.md`: "Repo location: PDS (primary and only copy)"). If the
33	PDS loses the repo — the exact "row present, bytes gone" class of failure that
34	motivated the blob backup (MM-394) — the user has their keys and their media but
35	nothing to reconstruct their timeline from.
36	
37	This plan adds a fourth self-custody copy: a periodic **CAR snapshot** of the repo,
38	written to the same iCloud Drive ubiquity container the blob mirror already uses.
39	Backup fetches the repo over the public, unauthenticated `com.atproto.sync.getRepo`
40	endpoint (no session needed, exactly like the blob backup's public reads), validates
41	the signed commit, and writes one atomically-replaced `.car` file per DID plus a
42	small manifest. The stored CAR is the canonical, directly-importable artifact — the
43	same bytes `com.atproto.repo.importRepo` and the wallet's existing migration
44	`transfer_repo` leg already consume — so it doubles as the account's portable exit.
45	
46	## The core design decision
47	
48	The obvious framing is a choice between two options:
49	
50	- **(A)** an occasional full-repo **CAR snapshot** tucked into the wallet, or
51	- **(B)** replicating the repo **tree** (individual IPLD blocks) into iCloud and
52	  **generating a CAR on-device** when the user wants to import to a new provider.
53	
54	These are not two independent features — they are the same feature with a different
55	**storage format**, and the "generate a CAR on-device" step is a *consequence* of (B)'s
56	storage choice, not a separate capability:
57	
58	- A **CAR is already the portable, importable artifact.** If we store a full CAR
59	  snapshot, we hold the exact bytes `importRepo` wants. There is nothing to
60	  "generate" at restore/export time — we read the file and hand it over.
61	- On-device CAR **generation** only becomes necessary if we deliberately store the
62	  repo as **unpacked, deduplicated blocks** (B), because then a CAR must be
63	  *reassembled* from the root CID (an MST walk) before any provider can accept it.
64	
65	So the real axis is: **store one replaceable CAR blob, or store a content-addressed
66	block tree and reassemble on demand.** Portability comes free either way. (B)'s only
67	genuine advantage is **incremental efficiency** — `getRepo?since=<rev>` lets the
68	wallet fetch only blocks added since the last backup, and deduplicated blocks avoid
69	re-storing unchanged history.
70	
71	That advantage is small in this system, because **the byte-heavy asset is blobs, and
72	blobs are backed up separately.** A repo *minus* its blobs is just records (text) and
73	MST nodes — typically a few MB even for a prolific poster. `getRepo` streams the
74	export block-by-block server-side with no size cap, so re-fetching the whole CAR on
75	each opportunistic pass is cheap. (B) pays for MST-walking, superseded-block-GC, and
76	a repo-engine dependency on-device to save bandwidth we don't meaningfully spend.
77	
78	## Recommendation
79	
80	**Build (A): a periodic full-CAR snapshot, cloned structurally from `blob_backup.rs`.**
81	Treat (B) as a documented future upgrade, reached only if measured repo sizes make
82	full snapshots painful — the server-side `getRepo?since=` support and repo-engine's
83	`collect_reachable_cids` + `build_car_from_cids` primitives make it a clean upgrade
84	that this plan deliberately leaves on the table.
85	
86	Rationale:
87	
88	1. **It completes the self-custody set with no new crypto surface.** Keys (already) +
89	   blobs (already) + repo CAR (this) = a user who can reconstruct their entire account
90	   from iCloud and their device alone.
91	2. **It reuses proven, already-shipped infrastructure end to end**: the CAR fetch
92	   (`PdsClient::fetch_repo_car`), the iCloud ubiquity-container mirror
93	   (`blob_backup::resolve_backup_root` + the `objc2`/`NSFileManager` path), the atomic
94	   temp-file+rename write, the per-DID manifest + opt-in-flag pattern, and the CAR
95	   import leg (`pds_client::import_repo`, driven today by `transfer_repo`).
96	3. **Integrity is free.** The CAR's declared root is the account's **signed commit**;
97	   content addressing makes the snapshot self-verifying, the same "content-addressed =
98	   trustless" property the blob mirror relies on. No encryption is needed — the repo
99	   is public data served by an `auth: none` endpoint, the identical posture already
100	   accepted for blobs (iCloud is E2EE only under Advanced Data Protection).
101	4. **No on-device CAR generation, no repo-engine dependency, no MST logic in the
102	   wallet.** The wallet fetches bytes and writes a file; the file *is* the export.
103	
104	## Definition of Done
105	
106	This plan is complete when:
107	
108	1. **A `repo_backup.rs` module** exists in `apps/identity-wallet/src-tauri/`, sibling
109	   to `blob_backup.rs`, exposing four fine-grained Tauri commands
110	   (`get_repo_backup_status`, `set_repo_backup_enabled`, `run_repo_backup`,
111	   `export_repo_backup`) plus one `pub(crate)` helper (`mirror_repo_car`) for the
112	   migration orchestrator's fallback source.
113	2. **Backup** is opt-in per DID (`{did}:repo-backup-enabled` Keychain slot), fetches
114	   the full CAR via the public `getRepo` on the DID's current hosting PDS, **validates
115	   the CAR's single root + commit signature before writing**, and atomically replaces
116	   `{root}/repo/{sanitized-did}.car` with a versioned manifest at
117	   `{root}/repo/{sanitized-did}.json` recording `{ rootCid, rev, sizeBytes,
118	   lastBackupAt }`. It runs on demand ("Back up now") and opportunistically on app
119	   open, mirroring the blob backup.
120	3. **The stored CAR is consumable by the existing import path.** The migration
121	   orchestrator's `transfer_repo` gains an iCloud-mirror fallback source
122	   (`repo_backup::mirror_repo_car`), the exact parallel of the blob drain's
123	   `mirror_fallback_blob` — so a migration whose *source* PDS can't serve `getRepo`
124	   heals from the user's iCloud copy, and the copy is proven wired into a real import.
125	4. **The mirror root and opt-in resolution are shared, not duplicated**, with
126	   `blob_backup` (both feed the same ubiquity container; `resolve_backup_root` and
127	   `BackupLocation` are reused).
128	5. **A "Back up your posts" surface** exists — either folded into the existing
129	   `MediaBackupScreen` (renamed to a combined backup screen) or a sibling screen —
130	   showing the opt-in, the snapshot size, and the last-backup time, and the
131	   opportunistic pass fires from `+page.svelte` on app open alongside the blob pass.
132	6. **Tests + parity**: Rust `_impl`/httpmock unit tests for the fetch→validate→write
133	   loop, manifest round-trip, and the mirror-fallback source; TypeScript IPC wrappers
134	   in `src/lib/ipc/` with a `RepoBackupError` union matching the Rust enum; a browser
135	   harness fake for the ubiquity path so the surface stays scriptable off-device;
136	   `pnpm check` green; the AGENTS.md contract + Bruno parity (no new routes — `getRepo`
137	   and `importRepo` already have `.bru` files) updated.
138	
139	## Acceptance Criteria
140	
141	### AC1: The repo is snapshotted to a user-controlled iCloud copy
142	- **AC1.1** With the feature opted in and iCloud Drive available, `run_repo_backup(did)`
143	  discovers the DID's current PDS, fetches the full CAR over public `getRepo`,
144	  validates it, and writes it atomically to `{root}/repo/{sanitized-did}.car`.
145	- **AC1.2** The manifest records the backed-up commit `rootCid`, repo `rev`, CAR
146	  `sizeBytes`, and `lastBackupAt`; `get_repo_backup_status` surfaces them for the UI.
147	- **AC1.3** On a real iOS device with iCloud Drive off, backup reports
148	  `BACKUP_UNAVAILABLE` — never a silent local-only fallback (matches blob backup).
149	- **AC1.4** A backup pass is idempotent: re-running when the repo `rev` is unchanged
150	  re-writes the same snapshot without error (and may short-circuit on matching `rev`).
151	
152	### AC2: The snapshot is integrity-checked, never trusting the PDS blindly
153	- **AC2.1** A fetched CAR that fails validation (not exactly one root, unparseable
154	  framing, commit `version != 3`, commit `did` ≠ the backed-up DID, or a broken MST
155	  walk) is rejected as `CAR_INVALID` and the prior good snapshot is left in place.
156	- **AC2.2** The declared root is verified to be a signed commit before the snapshot is
157	  considered good (self-verifying via content addressing).
158	
159	### AC3: The stored CAR restores/exports through the existing import machinery
160	- **AC3.1** `export_repo_backup(did)` reads and re-validates the stored CAR and returns
161	  its bytes (and manifest metadata) for a caller to import.
162	- **AC3.2** `migration_orchestrator::transfer_repo` falls back to
163	  `repo_backup::mirror_repo_car(did)` when the migration source PDS cannot serve
164	  `getRepo`, importing the iCloud copy instead — the repo twin of the blob drain's
165	  `mirror_fallback_blob`.
166	- **AC3.3** The fallback is used only when the mirror holds a CID/commit-valid CAR for
167	  the DID; otherwise the transfer surfaces the original source failure unchanged.
168	
169	### AC4: Opt-in, opportunistic, and shared with the blob backup
170	- **AC4.1** Opt-in is per DID via `{did}:repo-backup-enabled`; `IdentityStore::remove_identity`
171	  cleans the slot up (added to its per-DID suffix list).
172	- **AC4.2** `+page.svelte` fires a silent, fire-and-forget `runRepoBackup(did)` pass on
173	  app open for every opted-in identity, alongside the existing blob pass.
174	- **AC4.3** `resolve_backup_root`/`BackupLocation` are shared with `blob_backup`, not
175	  re-implemented; both features write under the same ubiquity container.
176	
177	### AC5: The surface is honest about size and scriptable off-device
178	- **AC5.1** The backup surface always shows the snapshot size before and after opt-in
179	  (iCloud's free tier is a shared 5 GB), and the last-backup time.
180	- **AC5.2** A browser-harness fake covers the ubiquity path (via `EZPDS_..._DIR` env
181	  override) so every state is reachable in fake mode; the fake-handler-coverage test
182	  passes for the new commands.
183	
184	## Architecture
185	
186	`repo_backup.rs` is a structural clone of `blob_backup.rs`, simplified because a repo
187	is **one artifact** rather than a set of content-addressed files — there is no
188	per-item diff loop, no pagination, no `MANIFEST_SAVE_EVERY` checkpointing. The whole
189	CAR is fetched, validated, and written in one atomic replace.
190	
191	**Storage layout** (under the shared backup root; blob uses `blobs/` + `manifests/`):
192	```
193	{root}/repo/{sanitized-did}.car     # the full CARv1 snapshot (declared root = signed commit)
194	{root}/repo/{sanitized-did}.json    # the manifest
195	```
196	`sanitized-did` reuses blob backup's `:` → `_` transform.
197	
198	**Manifest** (`RepoManifest`, `version: u32 = 1`, serde camelCase):
199	```rust
200	struct RepoManifest {
201	    version: u32,
202	    did: String,
203	    root_cid: String,       // the backed-up commit root CID
204	    rev: String,            // the repo revision (TID) at snapshot time
205	    size_bytes: u64,        // CAR length on disk
206	    last_backup_at: Option<String>,  // RFC 3339
207	}
208	```
209	
210	**Status readout** (`RepoBackupStatus`, serde camelCase) — the UI model:
211	```rust
212	struct RepoBackupStatus {
213	    enabled: bool,
214	    location: Option<BackupLocation>,   // reused from blob_backup
215	    root_cid: Option<String>,
216	    rev: Option<String>,
217	    size_bytes: u64,
218	    last_backup_at: Option<String>,
219	}
220	```
221	
222	**Command surface** (four Tauri commands + one `pub(crate)` helper):
223	
224	| Command | Does |
225	|---|---|
226	| `get_repo_backup_status(did)` | manifest → status readout (location, size, rev, last-backup) |
227	| `set_repo_backup_enabled(did, enabled)` | flip the `{did}:repo-backup-enabled` slot |
228	| `run_repo_backup(did)` | discover PDS → `fetch_repo_car` → **validate** → atomic write + manifest |
229	| `export_repo_backup(did)` | read + re-validate the stored CAR; return bytes + manifest for import |
230	| `mirror_repo_car(root, did) -> Option<Vec<u8>>` (`pub(crate)`) | the migration-orchestrator fallback source, twin of `blob_backup::mirror_fallback_blob` |
231	
232	**Backup flow** (`run_repo_backup`):
233	1. Resolve the backup root (`blob_backup::resolve_backup_root`; `BACKUP_UNAVAILABLE`
234	   when none).
235	2. `PdsClient::discover_pds(did)` → the DID's current hosting PDS URL (via plc.directory).
236	3. `PdsClient::fetch_repo_car(pds_url, did)` — the existing unauthenticated public
237	   fetch (`auth: none`, no session), reused verbatim from the migration path.
238	4. **Validate** the CAR: exactly one root, well-formed framing, commit `version == 3`,
239	   commit `did` matches, MST walk resolves. (This is the client-side twin of the
240	   server's `car_import::validate_car`; the wallet applies the same defensive checks
241	   the destination PDS would, so a corrupt fetch is never enshrined.)
242	5. Atomic temp-file + rename to `{root}/repo/{sanitized-did}.car`; write the manifest.
243	   Short-circuit when the fetched `rev` equals the manifest's (no-op re-backup).
244	
245	**Restore/export flow.** Unlike blobs — which restore by re-`uploadBlob` into a *live*
246	account — a repo import (`com.atproto.repo.importRepo`) requires a **deactivated**
247	account (it is the account-migration leg). So this plan does **not** ship a
248	"push my repo back to my live PDS" button; there is no such operation in ATProto.
249	Instead the stored CAR is made consumable two ways:
250	- **`export_repo_backup`** hands the validated bytes to a caller (diagnostics, a future
251	  disaster-recovery flow, or an "export my repo to a file" affordance).
252	- **`transfer_repo` mirror fallback** — the migration orchestrator, when its source PDS
253	  can't serve `getRepo`, sources the CAR from `repo_backup::mirror_repo_car` instead.
254	  This gets the backup *wired into a real import path in v1* and directly parallels how
255	  the blob drain already falls back to `mirror_fallback_blob`.
256	
257	**Error enum** (`RepoBackupError`, `#[serde(tag = "code", rename_all = "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE")]`):
258	`BACKUP_UNAVAILABLE`, `RATE_LIMITED`, `IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND`, `PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR`
259	(PDS discovery), `SERVER_ERROR`, `NETWORK_ERROR`, `STORAGE_ERROR`, `MANIFEST_CORRUPT`
260	(fail-closed, file preserved), `CAR_INVALID`, `KEYCHAIN_ERROR`. Note there is **no
261	`SESSION_LOCKED`** — backup reads a public endpoint and export reads local disk;
262	neither needs a full-access session (a genuine advantage over the blob restore path).
263	
264	## Existing Patterns
265	
266	This design copies patterns already established in the wallet:
267	
268	- **`blob_backup.rs` as the structural template** — opt-in per-DID Keychain slot,
269	  `resolve_backup_root` order (env override → iCloud ubiquity container → device with
270	  iCloud off = unavailable → local dev fallback), atomic temp+rename writes, versioned
271	  per-DID manifest, fail-closed corrupt manifest, opportunistic pass on app open,
272	  SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE error enum. `repo_backup` reuses `resolve_backup_root`,
273	  `BackupLocation`, and the `BACKUP_DIR_ENV` override directly.
274	- **The migration `transfer_repo` leg** already does `fetch_repo_car(source) →
275	  import_repo(dest)` (`migration_orchestrator.rs:658` `transfer_repo_impl`). The backup
276	  fetch is the first half of that, and the mirror fallback slots into it exactly like
277	  the blob drain's does.
278	- **`mirror_fallback_blob`** (`blob_backup.rs:876`, `pub(crate) async fn … -> Option<Vec<u8>>`)
279	  is the precise shape for `mirror_repo_car`.
280	- **Server-side CAR primitives already exist and need no change**: `getRepo`
281	  (`crates/pds/src/routes/get_repo.rs`, streamed, `auth: none`, no size cap) and
282	  `importRepo` (`crates/pds/src/routes/import_repo.rs`, deactivated account, 100 MiB
283	  cap). Both already have `.bru` fixtures, so `just bruno-check` needs nothing new.
284	- **The browser-harness fake + coverage test** — every `$lib/ipc` command needs a
285	  handler in `src/lib/harness/registry.ts`; the new commands get fakes driven by the
286	  `EZPDS_..._DIR` env override, same as the blob backup's harness treatment.
287	
288	## Implementation Phases
289	
290	### Phase 1: `repo_backup.rs` core — status, opt-in, backup, validate
291	The module, the manifest/status/error types, the four command cores as `_impl`
292	functions (Tauri-`State`-free, httpmock-tested), reusing `blob_backup::resolve_backup_root`.
293	CAR validation ported as the client twin of `car_import::validate_car`. **Done when**
294	`_impl` tests cover fetch→validate→atomic-write, the rev short-circuit, a rejected
295	`CAR_INVALID` fetch leaving the prior snapshot intact, and manifest round-trip.
296	
297	### Phase 2: Migration mirror-fallback wiring
298	`mirror_repo_car` + a fallback branch in `transfer_repo_impl` that tries the iCloud
299	CAR when the source `getRepo` fails (mirroring the blob drain). **Done when** an
300	integration test drives `transfer_repo` with a failing source and a populated mirror
301	and sees the import succeed from iCloud.
302	
303	### Phase 3: Commands + IPC + AGENTS.md
304	Register the commands in `lib.rs`; add `src/lib/ipc/repo-backup.ts` typed wrappers +
305	`RepoBackupError` union; add the `{did}:repo-backup-enabled` suffix to
306	`IdentityStore::remove_identity`'s cleanup list; extend the AGENTS.md `ipc.ts` exports
307	and module contract. **Done when** `pnpm check` passes and the error unions match.
308	
309	### Phase 4: UI surface + opportunistic pass + harness fake
310	Fold a "Back up your posts" section into `MediaBackupScreen` (or a sibling screen) with
311	size + last-backup shown; fire `runRepoBackup` opportunistically on app open in
312	`+page.svelte`; add the harness registry fakes + scenario. **Done when** the surface is
313	reachable in fake mode and the registry-coverage test passes.
314	
315	## Issue breakdown
316	
317	The work is split so the self-contained backup ships and reviews independently of the
318	migration-orchestrator wiring — the same split the blob backup used (MM-434 backup /
319	MM-446 migration fallback):
320	
321	- **MM-447** — the backup feature: `repo_backup.rs` (backup + validate +
322	  `export_repo_backup`), IPC, UI, harness, tests. Implementation Phases 1, 3, 4.
323	- **MM-448** — the `transfer_repo` iCloud-mirror fallback source (`mirror_repo_car`),
324	  Phase 2. Blocked by MM-447; the repo twin of MM-446.
325	- **MM-449** — background repo-backup passes via `BGProcessingTask`, sharing MM-444's
326	  mechanism. Blocked by MM-447.
327	- **MM-451** — the sovereign disaster-recovery flow (below): rebuild the account from
328	  the iCloud backups when the source PDS is gone. Blocked by MM-447.
329	- **MM-450** — block-level incremental storage (Option B, below): an icebox
330	  optimization, filed but trigger-gated on measured repo size. Related to MM-447.
331	
332	## Additional Considerations (sharp edges)
333	
334	**The disaster case (source PDS gone) is a follow-on — and it needs no PDS-side
335	change.** See the "Sovereign disaster-recovery flow" section below (MM-451): the wallet
336	can rebuild the account entirely client-side, because it holds `rotationKeys[0]` and can
337	enroll a self-controlled `atproto` signing key then mint the `createAccount` service-auth
338	JWT offline. This plan delivers the backup (MM-447) and migration mirror-fallback
339	(MM-448) first; MM-451 layers on the source-independent rebuild.
340	
341	**A CAR is records, not blobs.** The MST references blobs by CID but does not contain
342	their bytes. A full account restore is therefore **import the repo CAR (this backup) +
343	re-upload blobs (the existing blob mirror, via `listMissingBlobs`)** — the two backups
344	are complementary and together are the whole account. They are captured independently,
345	so a snapshot can reference a not-yet-mirrored blob (or vice versa); content addressing
346	makes this safely eventually-consistent (`listMissingBlobs` reconciles on import), but
347	the snapshots are not a single atomic point-in-time.
348	
349	**Import caps at 100 MiB** (`MAX_IMPORT_CAR_BYTES`) while `getRepo` export has no cap.
350	A repo of records rarely approaches this, but the status surface should show size, and
351	a snapshot exceeding the import cap is a known (documented) limitation for extreme
352	accounts — another data point that would argue for (B)'s incremental model if it ever
353	bites.
354	
355	**Encryption / privacy.** None is added: the repo is public data (`getRepo` is
356	`auth: none`), so plaintext-in-iCloud is the same posture already accepted for the blob
357	mirror. The mirror is Files-app-visible, reinforcing user-legible sovereignty.
358	
359	**Entitlements ride the existing template.** The iCloud container
360	(`iCloud.dev.malpercio.identitywallet`) and `Entitlements.ios.plist` are already in
361	place for the blob backup; repo backup writes under the same container and needs no new
362	entitlement, capability, or `just ios-template-check`/`ios-check` change.
363	
364	## Sovereign disaster-recovery flow (resolved design — MM-451)
365	
366	The credible-exit *guarantee*: rebuild the account on a new (or the same) PDS from the
367	iCloud backups **when the source PDS is gone or uncooperative** — with no dependency on
368	the old PDS. This upgrades the backup from a migration convenience to a real sovereignty
369	guarantee, and — the key resolution of this design session — **it needs no PDS-side
370	change.** It is the ATProto "adversarial migration" pattern (see the account-migration
371	guide's offline-auth path and D. Buchanan's "Adversarial ATProto PDS Migration"),
372	automated by a wallet that already holds the did:plc rotation key.
373	
374	**Why no PDS-side change.** `com.atproto.server.createAccount` is authorized by a
375	service-auth JWT signed with the DID's current `atproto` signing key. Normally that JWT
376	comes from the source PDS (`getServiceAuth`). But because the wallet holds
377	`rotationKeys[0]`, it can first enroll a **self-controlled** `atproto` signing key via a
378	device-key-signed PLC op, then **mint the JWT offline** itself. The destination PDS runs
379	the *standard* migration `createAccount` path and verifies the JWT against the
380	self-controlled key it resolves from plc.directory — so this works against any PDS, not
381	just Custos ("exit anywhere").
382	
383	**Flow — two guarded PLC ops, `createAccount`+import sandwiched between:**
384	1. **PLC op #1** (device-key-signed, direct to plc.directory): enroll a fresh
385	   self-controlled `atproto` signing key. (Buchanan bundles the `services.atproto_pds`
386	   repoint into this same op; reusing `migrate.rs` we may instead defer the repoint to
387	   op #2 — an implementation choice.) The strict guard preserves the wallet device key at
388	   `rotationKeys[0]`.
389	2. **Poll the plc.directory audit log** until op #1 is globally visible — `createAccount`
390	   cannot verify the offline JWT before the signing-key change propagates.
391	3. **Mint the service-auth JWT offline** with the self-controlled key:
392	   `iss = <account DID>`, `aud = did:web:<dest host>`,
393	   `lxm = com.atproto.server.createAccount`, ~3600s.
394	4. **`createAccount`** (deactivated) on the destination with the JWT → Bearer session.
395	5. **`importRepo`** from the iCloud CAR (`export_repo_backup`/`mirror_repo_car`), **drain
396	   blobs** from the iCloud mirror (`mirror_fallback_blob`), **`putPreferences`** if backed
397	   up.
398	6. **PLC op #2** (device-key-signed): adopt the destination's recommended rotation +
399	   `atproto` keys (`reserveSigningKey`/`getRecommendedDidCredentials`), handing
400	   commit-signing to the destination — **still preserving the wallet device key at
401	   `rotationKeys[0]`, at the front.**
402	7. **`activateAccount`** on the destination.
403	
404	**Reuse map.** *New:* offline service-auth JWT minting with a wallet-held key; a
405	wallet-*submitted* signing-key-enroll PLC op (a sovereign variant of `rotate_repo_key.rs`,
406	which today routes through the live PDS); the audit-log propagation poll. *Reused:*
407	`migrate.rs` op-building + strict guard for the identity legs; the migration
408	orchestrator's `createAccount`/`importRepo`/blob-drain/`activateAccount`; MM-448 (repo
409	mirror source) + MM-446 (blob mirror source).
410	
411	**Safety.** The strict allowlist guard must preserve the wallet's rotation key in *both*
412	ops — Buchanan's central warning is that accidentally dropping your own rotation key
413	permanently locks you out, and our `guard_migration_op`-style allowlists are exactly that
414	safeguard (already how the wallet's claim/migrate/handle/rotate ops stay honest). The
415	account stays deactivated (inert, not servable) until step 7; a stolen device key
416	attempting this is caught by `plc_monitor` + the 72-hour recovery-override window.
417	
418	**Edge case.** If the old PDS served the account's handle domain and is offline, the
419	handle won't resolve — the flow must let the user fall back to a destination-served handle
420	(e.g. `<handle>.<dest host>`).
421	
422	## Block-level incremental storage — deferred (Option B — MM-450)
423	
424	Filed as a trigger-gated icebox, not a discussion item. Store the repo as individual
425	content-addressed IPLD blocks and fetch only new blocks via `getRepo?since=<rev>`
426	(server-side support already exists), reassembling a CAR on-device from the current root
427	(`collect_reachable_cids` + `build_car_from_cids`, a repo-engine dep in the wallet). The
428	trigger to build it: measured repo sizes (the status surface shows snapshot size) where
429	re-fetching a full CAR on each pass is a real battery/bandwidth cost. Until then, the
430	full-CAR snapshot is simpler and cheap, because the byte-heavy asset (blobs) is mirrored
431	separately.
432	
433	## Glossary
434	
435	- **CAR (Content Addressable aRchive)**: the `application/vnd.ipld.car` binary format
436	  that packages a whole repo (signed commit + MST nodes + record blocks) in one
437	  transfer; the unit `getRepo` exports and `importRepo` imports.
438	- **MST (Merkle Search Tree)**: the tree ATProto stores repo records in; its nodes and
439	  the records are DAG-CBOR IPLD blocks addressed by CID.
440	- **Repo / commit / rev**: the repo's head is a **signed commit** naming a root CID; its
441	  **rev** is a TID revision that advances on every write and drives `getRepo?since=`.
442	- **Ubiquity container**: the app's iCloud Drive directory
443	  (`NSFileManager.URLForUbiquityContainerIdentifier`), reached from Rust via
444	  `objc2-foundation`; iOS syncs anything written to its `Documents/` and it is
445	  Files-app-visible. The blob mirror and this repo mirror share it.
446	- **`getRepo` / `importRepo`**: `com.atproto.sync.getRepo` (public, streamed, full or
447	  `since`-incremental CAR export) and `com.atproto.repo.importRepo` (imports a CAR into
448	  a **deactivated** account — the migration leg).
449	- **`fetch_repo_car`**: `PdsClient::fetch_repo_car(pds_url, did)`, the wallet's existing
450	  unauthenticated CAR fetch (`pds_client.rs:1277`), reused by this backup.
451	- **Mirror fallback**: the pattern where the migration transfer substitutes a
452	  CID/commit-verified local iCloud copy when the source PDS can't serve the asset —
453	  shipped for blobs as `mirror_fallback_blob`, added here for the repo as
454	  `mirror_repo_car`.
455	- **Service-auth JWT**: the short-lived token that authorizes `createAccount` for an
456	  existing DID, signed with the DID's `atproto` signing key and carrying `iss`
457	  (account DID), `aud` (destination PDS `did:web`), and `lxm`
458	  (`com.atproto.server.createAccount`). Normally minted by the source PDS
459	  (`getServiceAuth`); in disaster recovery the wallet mints it **offline** after enrolling
460	  a self-controlled signing key.
461	- **Adversarial migration**: moving an account off a PDS without that PDS's cooperation,
462	  by rotating the identity's `atproto` signing key to one the user controls and minting
463	  the migration credentials locally. The basis for the sovereign disaster-recovery flow
464	  (MM-451).
465	- **Rotation-key guard**: the strict pre-sign allowlist (`guard_migration_op` and
466	  siblings) that proves a wallet-built PLC op preserves the device key at
467	  `rotationKeys[0]` and changes only what it should — the safeguard against the
468	  "accidentally locked myself out" failure the adversarial-migration write-up warns of.

# Wallet-Held MST Repo Backup to iCloud

**Status: core shipped (MM-447, 2026-07-23 — PR #394, in v0.7.2). Follow-ons open;
plan retained for them.** This plan proposed — and the wallet now ships — a
`repo_backup.rs` module in the identity wallet that mirrors a user's ATProto repo
(their signed commit + MST + records — the CAR) into their iCloud Drive, as the
sibling of the user-held blob backup (`blob_backup.rs`, MM-434). It closed the last
gap in the wallet's self-custody story: until this landed, the repo was the one
account asset that lived *only* on the PDS.

What shipped under MM-447 (the "Definition of Done" below, minus item 3's migration
wiring): the four fine-grained Tauri commands + the `pub(crate) mirror_repo_car`
helper, opt-in per DID, the public-`getRepo` fetch with client-side CAR validation
before write, the shared iCloud root reused from `blob_backup`, and the "Back up your
posts" section folded into the Media Backup screen. What is **not** yet built, tracked
as follow-ons (see the sections below): consuming `mirror_repo_car` from the migration
`transfer_repo` drain (MM-448); background repo passes via `BGProcessingTask` (MM-449,
the repo sibling of the media sweep — repo backup is currently on-demand + opportunistic
on app open only, never off-foreground); block-level incremental storage (MM-450,
deferred / on ice); and the sovereign disaster-recovery rebuild (MM-451). This file
stays in `design-plans/` rather than moving to `archive/` because those follow-ons still
reference its design.

## Summary

The wallet already gives a user three self-controlled copies of the pieces of their
identity: the **keys** (device key in the Secure Enclave, recovery Share 1 in the
iCloud Keychain), and the **blobs** (media mirrored to iCloud Drive by
`blob_backup.rs`). The one asset with no user-held copy is the **repo** — the signed
commit + Merkle Search Tree + record blocks that hold every post, like, follow, and
profile edit. It lives on the PDS as the primary and only copy
(`docs/pds-architecture.md`: "Repo location: PDS (primary and only copy)"). If the
PDS loses the repo — the exact "row present, bytes gone" class of failure that
motivated the blob backup (MM-394) — the user has their keys and their media but
nothing to reconstruct their timeline from.

This plan adds a fourth self-custody copy: a periodic **CAR snapshot** of the repo,
written to the same iCloud Drive ubiquity container the blob mirror already uses.
Backup fetches the repo over the public, unauthenticated `com.atproto.sync.getRepo`
endpoint (no session needed, exactly like the blob backup's public reads), validates
the signed commit, and writes one atomically-replaced `.car` file per DID plus a
small manifest. The stored CAR is the canonical, directly-importable artifact — the
same bytes `com.atproto.repo.importRepo` and the wallet's existing migration
`transfer_repo` leg already consume — so it doubles as the account's portable exit.

## The core design decision

The obvious framing is a choice between two options:

- **(A)** an occasional full-repo **CAR snapshot** tucked into the wallet, or
- **(B)** replicating the repo **tree** (individual IPLD blocks) into iCloud and
  **generating a CAR on-device** when the user wants to import to a new provider.

These are not two independent features — they are the same feature with a different
**storage format**, and the "generate a CAR on-device" step is a *consequence* of (B)'s
storage choice, not a separate capability:

- A **CAR is already the portable, importable artifact.** If we store a full CAR
  snapshot, we hold the exact bytes `importRepo` wants. There is nothing to
  "generate" at restore/export time — we read the file and hand it over.
- On-device CAR **generation** only becomes necessary if we deliberately store the
  repo as **unpacked, deduplicated blocks** (B), because then a CAR must be
  *reassembled* from the root CID (an MST walk) before any provider can accept it.

So the real axis is: **store one replaceable CAR blob, or store a content-addressed
block tree and reassemble on demand.** Portability comes free either way. (B)'s only
genuine advantage is **incremental efficiency** — `getRepo?since=<rev>` lets the
wallet fetch only blocks added since the last backup, and deduplicated blocks avoid
re-storing unchanged history.

That advantage is small in this system, because **the byte-heavy asset is blobs, and
blobs are backed up separately.** A repo *minus* its blobs is just records (text) and
MST nodes — typically a few MB even for a prolific poster. `getRepo` streams the
export block-by-block server-side with no size cap, so re-fetching the whole CAR on
each opportunistic pass is cheap. (B) pays for MST-walking, superseded-block-GC, and
a repo-engine dependency on-device to save bandwidth we don't meaningfully spend.

## Recommendation

**Build (A): a periodic full-CAR snapshot, cloned structurally from `blob_backup.rs`.**
Treat (B) as a documented future upgrade, reached only if measured repo sizes make
full snapshots painful — the server-side `getRepo?since=` support and repo-engine's
`collect_reachable_cids` + `build_car_from_cids` primitives make it a clean upgrade
that this plan deliberately leaves on the table.

Rationale:

1. **It completes the self-custody set with no new crypto surface.** Keys (already) +
   blobs (already) + repo CAR (this) = a user who can reconstruct their entire account
   from iCloud and their device alone.
2. **It reuses proven, already-shipped infrastructure end to end**: the CAR fetch
   (`PdsClient::fetch_repo_car`), the iCloud ubiquity-container mirror
   (`blob_backup::resolve_backup_root` + the `objc2`/`NSFileManager` path), the atomic
   temp-file+rename write, the per-DID manifest + opt-in-flag pattern, and the CAR
   import leg (`pds_client::import_repo`, driven today by `transfer_repo`).
3. **Integrity is free.** The CAR's declared root is the account's **signed commit**;
   content addressing makes the snapshot self-verifying, the same "content-addressed =
   trustless" property the blob mirror relies on. No encryption is needed — the repo
   is public data served by an `auth: none` endpoint, the identical posture already
   accepted for blobs (iCloud is E2EE only under Advanced Data Protection).
4. **No on-device CAR generation, no repo-engine dependency, no MST logic in the
   wallet.** The wallet fetches bytes and writes a file; the file *is* the export.

This plan is complete when:

1. **A `repo_backup.rs` module** exists in `apps/identity-wallet/src-tauri/`, sibling

## Acceptance Criteria

### AC1: The repo is snapshotted to a user-controlled iCloud copy
- **AC1.1** With the feature opted in and iCloud Drive available, `run_repo_backup(did)`
  discovers the DID's current PDS, fetches the full CAR over public `getRepo`,
  validates it, and writes it atomically to `{root}/repo/{sanitized-did}.car`.
- **AC1.2** The manifest records the backed-up commit `rootCid`, repo `rev`, CAR
  `sizeBytes`, and `lastBackupAt`; `get_repo_backup_status` surfaces them for the UI.
- **AC1.3** On a real iOS device with iCloud Drive off, backup reports
  `BACKUP_UNAVAILABLE` — never a silent local-only fallback (matches blob backup).
- **AC1.4** A backup pass is idempotent: re-running when the repo `rev` is unchanged
  re-writes the same snapshot without error (and may short-circuit on matching `rev`).

### AC2: The snapshot is integrity-checked, never trusting the PDS blindly
- **AC2.1** A fetched CAR that fails validation (not exactly one root, unparseable
  framing, commit `version != 3`, commit `did` ≠ the backed-up DID, or a broken MST
  walk) is rejected as `CAR_INVALID` and the prior good snapshot is left in place.
- **AC2.2** The declared root is verified to be a signed commit before the snapshot is
  considered good (self-verifying via content addressing).

### AC3: The stored CAR restores/exports through the existing import machinery
- **AC3.1** `export_repo_backup(did)` reads and re-validates the stored CAR and returns
  its bytes (and manifest metadata) for a caller to import.
- **AC3.2** `migration_orchestrator::transfer_repo` falls back to
  `repo_backup::mirror_repo_car(did)` when the migration source PDS cannot serve
  `getRepo`, importing the iCloud copy instead — the repo twin of the blob drain's
  `mirror_fallback_blob`.
- **AC3.3** The fallback is used only when the mirror holds a CID/commit-valid CAR for
  the DID; otherwise the transfer surfaces the original source failure unchanged.

### AC4: Opt-in, opportunistic, and shared with the blob backup
- **AC4.1** Opt-in is per DID via `{did}:repo-backup-enabled`; `IdentityStore::remove_identity`
  cleans the slot up (added to its per-DID suffix list).
- **AC4.2** `+page.svelte` fires a silent, fire-and-forget `runRepoBackup(did)` pass on
  app open for every opted-in identity, alongside the existing blob pass.
- **AC4.3** `resolve_backup_root`/`BackupLocation` are shared with `blob_backup`, not
  re-implemented; both features write under the same ubiquity container.

### AC5: The surface is honest about size and scriptable off-device
- **AC5.1** The backup surface always shows the snapshot size before and after opt-in
  (iCloud's free tier is a shared 5 GB), and the last-backup time.
- **AC5.2** A browser-harness fake covers the ubiquity path (via `EZPDS_..._DIR` env
  override) so every state is reachable in fake mode; the fake-handler-coverage test
  passes for the new commands.

## Architecture

`repo_backup.rs` is a structural clone of `blob_backup.rs`, simplified because a repo
is **one artifact** rather than a set of content-addressed files — there is no
per-item diff loop, no pagination, no `MANIFEST_SAVE_EVERY` checkpointing. The whole
CAR is fetched, validated, and written in one atomic replace.

**Storage layout** (under the shared backup root; blob uses `blobs/` + `manifests/`):
```
{root}/repo/{sanitized-did}.car     # the full CARv1 snapshot (declared root = signed commit)
{root}/repo/{sanitized-did}.json    # the manifest
```
`sanitized-did` reuses blob backup's `:` → `_` transform.

**Manifest** (`RepoManifest`, `version: u32 = 1`, serde camelCase):
```rust
struct RepoManifest {
    version: u32,
    did: String,
    root_cid: String,       // the backed-up commit root CID
    rev: String,            // the repo revision (TID) at snapshot time
    size_bytes: u64,        // CAR length on disk
    last_backup_at: Option<String>,  // RFC 3339
}
```

**Status readout** (`RepoBackupStatus`, serde camelCase) — the UI model:
```rust
struct RepoBackupStatus {
    enabled: bool,
    location: Option<BackupLocation>,   // reused from blob_backup
    root_cid: Option<String>,
    rev: Option<String>,
    size_bytes: u64,
    last_backup_at: Option<String>,
}
```

**Command surface** (four Tauri commands + one `pub(crate)` helper):

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `get_repo_backup_status(did)` | manifest → status readout (location, size, rev, last-backup) |
| `set_repo_backup_enabled(did, enabled)` | flip the `{did}:repo-backup-enabled` slot |
| `run_repo_backup(did)` | discover PDS → `fetch_repo_car` → **validate** → atomic write + manifest |
| `export_repo_backup(did)` | read + re-validate the stored CAR; return bytes + manifest for import |
| `mirror_repo_car(root, did) -> Option<Vec<u8>>` (`pub(crate)`) | the migration-orchestrator fallback source, twin of `blob_backup::mirror_fallback_blob` |

**Backup flow** (`run_repo_backup`):
1. Resolve the backup root (`blob_backup::resolve_backup_root`; `BACKUP_UNAVAILABLE`
   when none).
2. `PdsClient::discover_pds(did)` → the DID's current hosting PDS URL (via plc.directory).
3. `PdsClient::fetch_repo_car(pds_url, did)` — the existing unauthenticated public
   fetch (`auth: none`, no session), reused verbatim from the migration path.
4. **Validate** the CAR: exactly one root, well-formed framing, commit `version == 3`,
   commit `did` matches, MST walk resolves. (This is the client-side twin of the
   server's `car_import::validate_car`; the wallet applies the same defensive checks
   the destination PDS would, so a corrupt fetch is never enshrined.)
5. Atomic temp-file + rename to `{root}/repo/{sanitized-did}.car`; write the manifest.
   Short-circuit when the fetched `rev` equals the manifest's (no-op re-backup).

**Restore/export flow.** Unlike blobs — which restore by re-`uploadBlob` into a *live*
account — a repo import (`com.atproto.repo.importRepo`) requires a **deactivated**
account (it is the account-migration leg). So this plan does **not** ship a
"push my repo back to my live PDS" button; there is no such operation in ATProto.
Instead the stored CAR is made consumable two ways:
- **`export_repo_backup`** hands the validated bytes to a caller (diagnostics, a future
  disaster-recovery flow, or an "export my repo to a file" affordance).
- **`transfer_repo` mirror fallback** — the migration orchestrator, when its source PDS
  can't serve `getRepo`, sources the CAR from `repo_backup::mirror_repo_car` instead.
  This gets the backup *wired into a real import path in v1* and directly parallels how
  the blob drain already falls back to `mirror_fallback_blob`.

**Error enum** (`RepoBackupError`, `#[serde(tag = "code", rename_all = "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE")]`):
`BACKUP_UNAVAILABLE`, `RATE_LIMITED`, `IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND`, `PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR`
(PDS discovery), `SERVER_ERROR`, `NETWORK_ERROR`, `STORAGE_ERROR`, `MANIFEST_CORRUPT`
(fail-closed, file preserved), `CAR_INVALID`, `KEYCHAIN_ERROR`. Note there is **no
`SESSION_LOCKED`** — backup reads a public endpoint and export reads local disk;
neither needs a full-access session (a genuine advantage over the blob restore path).

## Existing Patterns

This design copies patterns already established in the wallet:

- **`blob_backup.rs` as the structural template** — opt-in per-DID Keychain slot,
  `resolve_backup_root` order (env override → iCloud ubiquity container → device with
  iCloud off = unavailable → local dev fallback), atomic temp+rename writes, versioned
  per-DID manifest, fail-closed corrupt manifest, opportunistic pass on app open,
  SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE error enum. `repo_backup` reuses `resolve_backup_root`,
  `BackupLocation`, and the `BACKUP_DIR_ENV` override directly.
- **The migration `transfer_repo` leg** already does `fetch_repo_car(source) →
  import_repo(dest)` (`migration_orchestrator.rs:658` `transfer_repo_impl`). The backup
  fetch is the first half of that, and the mirror fallback slots into it exactly like
  the blob drain's does.
- **`mirror_fallback_blob`** (`blob_backup.rs:876`, `pub(crate) async fn … -> Option<Vec<u8>>`)
  is the precise shape for `mirror_repo_car`.
- **Server-side CAR primitives already exist and need no change**: `getRepo`
  (`crates/pds/src/routes/get_repo.rs`, streamed, `auth: none`, no size cap) and
  `importRepo` (`crates/pds/src/routes/import_repo.rs`, deactivated account, 100 MiB
  cap). Both already have `.bru` fixtures, so `just bruno-check` needs nothing new.
- **The browser-harness fake + coverage test** — every `$lib/ipc` command needs a
  handler in `src/lib/harness/registry.ts`; the new commands get fakes driven by the
  `EZPDS_..._DIR` env override, same as the blob backup's harness treatment.

## Additional Considerations (sharp edges)

**The disaster case (source PDS gone) is a follow-on — and it needs no PDS-side
change.** See the "Sovereign disaster-recovery flow" section below (MM-451): the wallet
can rebuild the account entirely client-side, because it holds `rotationKeys[0]` and can
enroll a self-controlled `atproto` signing key then mint the `createAccount` service-auth
JWT offline. This plan delivers the backup (MM-447) and migration mirror-fallback
(MM-448) first; MM-451 layers on the source-independent rebuild.

**A CAR is records, not blobs.** The MST references blobs by CID but does not contain
their bytes. A full account restore is therefore **import the repo CAR (this backup) +
re-upload blobs (the existing blob mirror, via `listMissingBlobs`)** — the two backups
are complementary and together are the whole account. They are captured independently,
so a snapshot can reference a not-yet-mirrored blob (or vice versa); content addressing
makes this safely eventually-consistent (`listMissingBlobs` reconciles on import), but
the snapshots are not a single atomic point-in-time.

**Import caps at 100 MiB** (`MAX_IMPORT_CAR_BYTES`) while `getRepo` export has no cap.
A repo of records rarely approaches this, but the status surface should show size, and
a snapshot exceeding the import cap is a known (documented) limitation for extreme
accounts — another data point that would argue for (B)'s incremental model if it ever
bites.

**Encryption / privacy.** None is added: the repo is public data (`getRepo` is
`auth: none`), so plaintext-in-iCloud is the same posture already accepted for the blob
mirror. The mirror is Files-app-visible, reinforcing user-legible sovereignty.

**Entitlements ride the existing template.** The iCloud container
(`iCloud.dev.malpercio.identitywallet`) and `Entitlements.ios.plist` are already in
place for the blob backup; repo backup writes under the same container and needs no new
entitlement, capability, or `just ios-template-check`/`ios-check` change.

## Sovereign disaster-recovery flow (resolved design — MM-451)

The credible-exit *guarantee*: rebuild the account on a new (or the same) PDS from the
iCloud backups **when the source PDS is gone or uncooperative** — with no dependency on
the old PDS. This upgrades the backup from a migration convenience to a real sovereignty
guarantee, and — the key resolution of this design session — **it needs no PDS-side
change.** It is the ATProto "adversarial migration" pattern (see the account-migration
guide's offline-auth path and D. Buchanan's "Adversarial ATProto PDS Migration"),
automated by a wallet that already holds the did:plc rotation key.

**Why no PDS-side change.** `com.atproto.server.createAccount` is authorized by a
service-auth JWT signed with the DID's current `atproto` signing key. Normally that JWT
comes from the source PDS (`getServiceAuth`). But because the wallet holds
`rotationKeys[0]`, it can first enroll a **self-controlled** `atproto` signing key via a
device-key-signed PLC op, then **mint the JWT offline** itself. The destination PDS runs
the *standard* migration `createAccount` path and verifies the JWT against the
self-controlled key it resolves from plc.directory — so this works against any PDS, not
just Custos ("exit anywhere").

**Flow — two guarded PLC ops, `createAccount`+import sandwiched between:**
1. **PLC op #1** (device-key-signed, direct to plc.directory): enroll a fresh
   self-controlled `atproto` signing key. (Buchanan bundles the `services.atproto_pds`
   repoint into this same op; reusing `migrate.rs` we may instead defer the repoint to
   op #2 — an implementation choice.) The strict guard preserves the wallet device key at
   `rotationKeys[0]`.
2. **Poll the plc.directory audit log** until op #1 is globally visible — `createAccount`
   cannot verify the offline JWT before the signing-key change propagates.
3. **Mint the service-auth JWT offline** with the self-controlled key:
   `iss = <account DID>`, `aud = did:web:<dest host>`,
   `lxm = com.atproto.server.createAccount`, ~3600s.
4. **`createAccount`** (deactivated) on the destination with the JWT → Bearer session.
5. **`importRepo`** from the iCloud CAR (`export_repo_backup`/`mirror_repo_car`), **drain
   blobs** from the iCloud mirror (`mirror_fallback_blob`), **`putPreferences`** if backed
   up.
6. **PLC op #2** (device-key-signed): adopt the destination's recommended rotation +
   `atproto` keys (`reserveSigningKey`/`getRecommendedDidCredentials`), handing
   commit-signing to the destination — **still preserving the wallet device key at
   `rotationKeys[0]`, at the front.**
7. **`activateAccount`** on the destination.

**Reuse map.** *New:* offline service-auth JWT minting with a wallet-held key; a
wallet-*submitted* signing-key-enroll PLC op (a sovereign variant of `rotate_repo_key.rs`,
which today routes through the live PDS); the audit-log propagation poll. *Reused:*
`migrate.rs` op-building + strict guard for the identity legs; the migration
orchestrator's `createAccount`/`importRepo`/blob-drain/`activateAccount`; MM-448 (repo
mirror source) + MM-446 (blob mirror source).

**Safety.** The strict allowlist guard must preserve the wallet's rotation key in *both*
ops — Buchanan's central warning is that accidentally dropping your own rotation key
permanently locks you out, and our `guard_migration_op`-style allowlists are exactly that
safeguard (already how the wallet's claim/migrate/handle/rotate ops stay honest). The
account stays deactivated (inert, not servable) until step 7; a stolen device key
attempting this is caught by `plc_monitor` + the 72-hour recovery-override window.

**Edge case.** If the old PDS served the account's handle domain and is offline, the
handle won't resolve — the flow must let the user fall back to a destination-served handle
(e.g. `<handle>.<dest host>`).

## Block-level incremental storage — deferred (Option B — MM-450)

Filed as a trigger-gated icebox, not a discussion item. Store the repo as individual
content-addressed IPLD blocks and fetch only new blocks via `getRepo?since=<rev>`
(server-side support already exists), reassembling a CAR on-device from the current root
(`collect_reachable_cids` + `build_car_from_cids`, a repo-engine dep in the wallet). The
trigger to build it: measured repo sizes (the status surface shows snapshot size) where
re-fetching a full CAR on each pass is a real battery/bandwidth cost. Until then, the
full-CAR snapshot is simpler and cheap, because the byte-heavy asset (blobs) is mirrored
separately.

## Glossary

- **CAR (Content Addressable aRchive)**: the `application/vnd.ipld.car` binary format
  that packages a whole repo (signed commit + MST nodes + record blocks) in one
  transfer; the unit `getRepo` exports and `importRepo` imports.
- **MST (Merkle Search Tree)**: the tree ATProto stores repo records in; its nodes and
  the records are DAG-CBOR IPLD blocks addressed by CID.
- **Repo / commit / rev**: the repo's head is a **signed commit** naming a root CID; its
  **rev** is a TID revision that advances on every write and drives `getRepo?since=`.
- **Ubiquity container**: the app's iCloud Drive directory
  (`NSFileManager.URLForUbiquityContainerIdentifier`), reached from Rust via
  `objc2-foundation`; iOS syncs anything written to its `Documents/` and it is
  Files-app-visible. The blob mirror and this repo mirror share it.
- **`getRepo` / `importRepo`**: `com.atproto.sync.getRepo` (public, streamed, full or
  `since`-incremental CAR export) and `com.atproto.repo.importRepo` (imports a CAR into
  a **deactivated** account — the migration leg).
- **`fetch_repo_car`**: `PdsClient::fetch_repo_car(pds_url, did)`, the wallet's existing
  unauthenticated CAR fetch (`pds_client.rs:1277`), reused by this backup.
- **Mirror fallback**: the pattern where the migration transfer substitutes a
  CID/commit-verified local iCloud copy when the source PDS can't serve the asset —
  shipped for blobs as `mirror_fallback_blob`, added here for the repo as
  `mirror_repo_car`.
- **Service-auth JWT**: the short-lived token that authorizes `createAccount` for an
  existing DID, signed with the DID's `atproto` signing key and carrying `iss`
  (account DID), `aud` (destination PDS `did:web`), and `lxm`
  (`com.atproto.server.createAccount`). Normally minted by the source PDS
  (`getServiceAuth`); in disaster recovery the wallet mints it **offline** after enrolling
  a self-controlled signing key.
- **Adversarial migration**: moving an account off a PDS without that PDS's cooperation,
  by rotating the identity's `atproto` signing key to one the user controls and minting
  the migration credentials locally. The basis for the sovereign disaster-recovery flow
  (MM-451).
- **Rotation-key guard**: the strict pre-sign allowlist (`guard_migration_op` and
  siblings) that proves a wallet-built PLC op preserves the device key at
  `rotationKeys[0]` and changes only what it should — the safeguard against the
  "accidentally locked myself out" failure the adversarial-migration write-up warns of.

# Obsign (identity-wallet) Mobile App

Last verified: 2026-07-08
Last updated: 2026-07-20

## Purpose

Tauri v2 iOS application — SvelteKit 2 + Svelte 5 frontend running in a native WKWebView, communicating with a Rust backend exclusively through Tauri's IPC bridge.

## Browser test harness (drive the app without a simulator)

The whole frontend runs in a plain desktop browser under `vite dev` — the only thing the
browser lacks is the Tauri `invoke()` seam, which the harness intercepts with Tauri's
official `mockIPC`. This lets an agent (or a human) reach every screen and reproduce any
state, including rare error states, without a Mac/Xcode/simulator. Design + acceptance
criteria: [docs/archive/design-plans/2026-07-12-browser-harness.md](../../docs/archive/design-plans/2026-07-12-browser-harness.md).

**Start it** (or use the `.claude/launch.json` config `wallet-harness` / `wallet-harness-proxy`):
- **Fake mode** (default, no backend needed): `pnpm --dir apps/identity-wallet dev:harness` → http://localhost:5173.
- **Proxy mode** (real thin-HTTP calls against a hermetic local PDS): in one terminal
  `cargo build -p pds` then `just harness-pds` (prints the URL + admin token); in another,
  `VITE_HARNESS_PDS_URL=<url> VITE_HARNESS_ADMIN_TOKEN=<token> pnpm --dir apps/identity-wallet dev:harness:proxy`.
- Plain `pnpm dev` never activates the harness (double-gated on `import.meta.env.DEV && VITE_HARNESS`);
  `pnpm check:harness-absence` proves it is tree-shaken out of production builds.

**`window.__harness` console API** (both modes):
- `.scenario(name)` — switch preset and reload (persists across reload). Presets:
  `fresh-install`, `one-identity`, `multi-identity`, `alert-active`, `migration-in-flight`,
  `agent-connected`, `app-password-minted`, plus the share-recovery matrix:
  `recover-escrow` (happy path A — iCloud Share 1 + zero-delay escrow release),
  `recover-sovereign` (happy path B — manual Share 3 entry; paste
  `state().recovery.fixtures.share3Words` or `.share3`), `recover-wrong-set`
  (`fixtures.wrongSet` → SHARE_SET_MISMATCH), `recover-corrupt-share`
  (`fixtures.corrupt` → SHARE_CHECKSUM), `recover-mismatch` (verification fails —
  shares don't match the identity), `recover-pending-delay` (24h escrow window; the
  second poll releases), `recover-cancelled` (pending release cancelled → uniform
  401 on poll), `recover-epilogue-resume` (launch resumes an interrupted rotation
  epilogue). `.scenarios` lists them.
- `.failNext(command, error)` — make the next call of `command` reject with a typed error,
  e.g. `window.__harness.failNext('create_account', { code: 'EXPIRED_CODE' })`.
- `.emit(event, payload)` — deliver a Tauri event to live `listen()` subscribers;
  `window.__harness.emit('auth_ready')` simulates the OAuth deep-link return.
- `.state()` — a read-only snapshot of the fake store. `.mode` is `'fake'` or `'proxy'`.

**Proxy mode is real only for the thin-HTTP subset** — `create_account` (mints + redeems a
real claim code, POSTs `/v1/accounts/mobile`) and `get_available_user_domains`
(describeServer). By the honest boundary, these stay **faked even in proxy mode** (heavy
Rust logic with no thin-HTTP form): the DID ceremony (`perform_did_ceremony`,
`*_did_web_ceremony`), OAuth completion (`prepare/complete_oauth_flow`), the migration
transfer legs (`transfer_repo`/`transfer_blobs`/…, `finalize_migration`), recovery/claim
PLC ops, and the agent surfaces (which need a real post-ceremony session the faked
ceremony never mints). Fidelity the browser can never cover: real Keychain/Secure-Enclave,
the biometric prompt, ASWebAuthenticationSession, WKWebView rendering, safe-area insets,
camera/QR — those stay simulator/device concerns.

**Fake handler coverage is enforced:** every command in `$lib/ipc` must have a handler in
`src/lib/harness/registry.ts` or `registry.test.ts` fails (`pnpm test`). Harness code lives
in `src/lib/harness/` (`install`/`registry`/`state`/`scenarios`/`control` + `proxy/`),
activated by `src/hooks.client.ts`.

## Contracts

### Frontend (SvelteKit 2 + Svelte 5)

**Exposes:**
- `src/lib/ipc/` — per-domain typed wrappers for all Tauri IPC commands, re-exported from `src/lib/ipc/index.ts`; import from `$lib/ipc` instead of calling `invoke()` directly. Exports: `createAccount()`, `performDIDCeremony()`, `registerHandle()`, `getAvailableUserDomains()`, `registerCreatedIdentity()`, `startOAuthFlow()`, `getPdsUrl()`, `savePdsUrl()`, `getAppearancePreference()`, `setAppearancePreference()`, `resolveIdentity()`, `authenticateSourcePds()`, `requestClaimVerification()`, `signAndVerifyClaim()`, `submitClaim()`, `listIdentities()`, `getStoredDidDoc()`, `getDeviceKeyId()`, `checkIdentityStatus()`, `buildRecoveryOverride()`, `submitRecoveryOverride()`, and their associated types (`CreateAccountResult`, `CreateAccountError`, `DIDCeremonyResult`, `DIDCeremonyError`, `RegisterHandleResult`, `RegisterHandleError`, `RegisterIdentityError`, `OAuthError`, `PdsConfigError`, `AppearancePreference`, `AppearanceError`, `IdentityInfo`, `VerifiedClaimOp`, `OpDiff`, `ServiceChange`, `ClaimResult`, `ResolveError`, `ClaimError`, `IdentityStoreError`, `UnauthorizedChange`, `IdentityStatus`, `SignedRecoveryOp`, `RecoveryError`, `SignedMigrationOp`, `MigrateError`) and migration wrappers (`buildMigrationOp()`, `submitMigrationOp()`) and outbound-migration orchestrator wrappers (`prepareMigration()`, `authenticateMigrationSource()`, `createDestinationAccount()`, `transferRepo()`, `transferBlobs(did, acceptLoss)`, `transferPreferences()`, `verifyImport()`, `armIdentityLeg()`, `finalizeMigration()`) with types (`AccountStatus`, `PreparedMigration`, `MigrationError`, `BlobLoss`, `BlobTransferDirection`), the sovereign change-handle wrappers (`getIdentityHandleDomains()`, `changeHandle()` — biometric-gated) with type `HandleChangeError`, and identity-removal wrappers (`requestIdentityRemoval()`, `confirmIdentityRemoval()`, `tombstoneIdentity()`, `listPendingRemovals()`, `forgetIdentityLocally()`) with types (`RemovalError`, `RemovalOutcome`), and the share-recovery wrappers (`startShareRecovery()`, `addRecoveryShare()`, `removeRecoveryShare()`, `initiateEscrowRelease()`, `requestEscrowRelease()`, `verifyRecoveryShares()`, `recoverIdentity()` — biometric-gated, `runRecoveryEpilogue()`, `getPendingRecoveryEpilogue()`, `confirmRecoveryBackup()`) with types (`ShareRecoveryError`, `CollectedShare`, `RecoveryTarget`, `EscrowReleaseStatus`, `RecoveredIdentity`, `RecoveryAnchor`, `EpilogueResult`, `PendingEpilogue`), and the media-backup wrappers (`getBlobBackupStatus()`, `setBlobBackupEnabled()`, `runBlobBackup()`, `restoreBlobBackup()` — biometric-gated, and the app-global background-sweep settings `getBackgroundBackupSettings()` / `setBackgroundBackupSettings()`) with types (`BlobBackupStatus`, `BlobBackupRunReport`, `BlobRestoreReport`, `BlobFailure`, `BackupLocation`, `BlobBackupError`, `BackgroundBackupSettings`, `BackgroundBackupError`), and the repo-backup wrappers (`getRepoBackupStatus()`, `setRepoBackupEnabled()`, `runRepoBackup()`, `exportRepoBackup()` — none biometric-gated; all read the public `getRepo` or local disk) with types (`RepoBackupStatus`, `RepoBackupRunReport`, `RepoExport`, `RepoBackupError`)
- `src/lib/components/onboarding/` — one screen component per step of the create / import / recover onboarding flows (the directory listing is the authoritative inventory; hand-counted lists here drifted twice)
- `src/lib/components/home/` — the home-surface screen components (the directory listing is the authoritative inventory) plus the DIDAvatar utility component (deterministic DID-derived hue circle). ChangeHandleScreen is the sovereign change-handle surface reached from DIDDocumentScreen's "Change handle" button (did:plc + device-key-as-root only): it loads the hosting PDS's served domains, pre-flights the session (`ensureIdentitySession`, passwordless `sovereignLogin` on `NEEDS_UNLOCK`), then runs the biometric-gated `changeHandle`. AppPasswordsScreen is the app-password surface reached from DIDDocumentScreen's "Sign in to Bluesky and other apps" button: it lists/mints/revokes the account's scoped app passwords via `SessionProvider::full_access_client` (SESSION_LOCKED → `sovereignLogin` + retry; mint and revoke are biometric-gated; the generated secret is shown once with copy and never persisted). MediaBackupScreen is the user-held blob-backup surface reached from DIDDocumentScreen's "Back up media" button: opt-in with the mirror size always shown, "Back up now" (incremental, CID-verified sync pass over public sync endpoints — no session), and a biometric-gated "Restore to server" (`uploadBlob` via `SessionProvider::full_access_client`; SESSION_LOCKED → `sovereignLogin` + retry), with per-blob failures listed rather than aborting the run. The same screen also holds a "Back up your posts" section (`repo_backup.rs`): opt-in with the snapshot size + last-backup shown, and "Back up posts now" (a full-CAR `getRepo` snapshot, validated client-side before it replaces the prior copy — no session, no biometric); there is no repo "restore" button (an `importRepo` needs a deactivated account, so restore flows through migration). `+page.svelte` fires silent opportunistic `runBlobBackup` **and** `runRepoBackup` passes on app open for opted-in identities (each on its own per-DID flag). MyAgentsScreen is the agent list; AgentDetailScreen is the per-agent sub-view (audit-trail paging + biometric-gated revoke) it renders on selection, its lifetime scoped to that selection. RemoveIdentityScreen is the permanent-removal flow (warn → emailed-code + password → biometric-gated hold-to-remove → progress, with a "tombstone pending, retry" state), reached from DIDDocumentScreen's destructive `onremove`
- `src/lib/appearance.ts` — in-app appearance override (System / Light / Dark): `normalizePreference()` / `toColorScheme()` (pure, tested by `appearance.test.ts`), `readLocalMirror()`, `initAppearance()` (launch-time reconcile: re-asserts the localStorage mirror, then reads the Keychain via IPC and lets it win), `setAppearance()` (applies the inline `color-scheme` override on `<html>` instantly, writes the mirror, then persists to the Keychain). The localStorage mirror (key `appearance-preference`) exists only so `src/app.html`'s inline `<head>` script can apply a forced appearance before first paint; the Keychain is the source of truth
- `src/lib/agent-scopes.ts` — plain-language descriptions of granular OAuth scope tokens for the agent-consent surfaces: `describeScope(token)` / `describeScopes(tokens)` return `{ summary, token, elevated }` (the raw token is always shown alongside the human sentence; `account:*`/`identity:*`/full-access grants are flagged `elevated`; an unknown token falls back to showing itself, never a vague label). Tested by `agent-scopes.test.ts`
- `src/lib/deadline.ts` — PLC recovery deadline utilities: `getDeadline(createdAt)` (adds 72h to ISO 8601 timestamp), `getUrgency(deadline)` (returns `'safe'` | `'warning'` | `'critical'` | `'expired'`), `formatCountdown(deadline)` (human-readable `"Xh Ym remaining"`). `Urgency` type exported. Thresholds: expired = 0, critical < 4h, warning < 24h, safe >= 24h
- `src/routes/+page.svelte` — root page: two-flow state machine starting at `mode_select`. **Create flow:** mode_select -> pds_config -> claim_code -> email -> handle -> password (every pre-submit step wires `onback` to the previous step) -> loading -> did_ceremony -> did_success -> shamir_backup -> handle_registration -> complete -> authenticating -> home (after handle_registration succeeds, `finishCreateFlow()` calls `registerCreatedIdentity()` to persist the new identity to `IdentityStore` so it appears in `IdentityListHome` — best-effort, never blocks the flow). **Import flow:** mode_select -> identity_input -> pds_auth -> email_verification -> review_operation -> claim_success -> home. **Home:** home -> identity_detail -> { change_handle | alert_detail -> recovery_override }. On mount, checks for existing identities via `listIdentities()` and skips to `home` if any exist. Registers a `visibilitychange` listener that calls `checkIdentityStatus()` when the app returns to foreground while on the `home` step

**Guarantees:**
- SSR is disabled globally (`ssr = false` in `src/routes/+layout.ts`); the frontend is a fully static SPA loaded from disk by WKWebView
- Build output lands in `dist/` (configured via `pages: 'dist'` in `svelte.config.js`)
- Frontend calls Tauri commands only through the `src/lib/ipc/` modules (imported from `$lib/ipc`) — no raw `invoke()` calls in page components
- PDS error codes from `create_account` are mapped back to the originating screen (e.g. EXPIRED_CODE -> claim_code step, EMAIL_TAKEN -> email step)

**Expects:**
- `pnpm install` has been run in `apps/identity-wallet/`
- Node.js 22.x is in PATH (provided by the Nix dev shell)

### Rust Backend (src-tauri/)

**Exposes:**
- `src/lib.rs::create_account(claim_code, email, handle) -> Result<CreateAccountResult, CreateAccountError>` — Tauri IPC command: gets or creates device key via `device_key::get_or_create()`, POSTs to PDS `/v1/accounts/mobile`, stores tokens in Keychain on success
- `src/lib.rs::perform_did_ceremony(handle: String, password: String) -> Result<DIDCeremonyResult, DIDCeremonyError>` — Tauri IPC command running the **client-share ceremony** (ceremony inversion): fetches the PDS signing key (GET /v1/repo-signing-key), loads-or-generates the client-side share set via `share_ceremony::load_or_create` (recovery seed + `derive_recovery_keypair` + 2-of-3 v2 envelope split, staged in the `ceremony-staging` Keychain slot BEFORE any network call so a retry reuses the identical set/set_id), builds the signed did:plc genesis op via `crypto::build_did_plc_genesis_op_multi_rotation_with_external_signer` with `rotationKeys = [device, recovery, PDS]` (ADR-0027) using the device key as signer, POSTs the op + password + `recoveryKey` + `escrowShare` (the Share 2 envelope — the only share Custos ever sees) to POST /v1/dids, persists DID + upgraded session token in Keychain, writes the wallet-generated Share 1 envelope to the per-DID slot `recovery-share-1:{did}` with a read-back verify (same convention as the re-key flow, so a second identity's ceremony cannot overwrite the first's Share 1), and returns `{ did, share3, share3Words }` to the frontend
- `src/lib.rs::confirm_share_backup(did: String) -> Result<(), ShareBackupError>` — Tauri IPC command: the ceremony teardown gate. Verifies the ceremony DID's Share 1 is durably present in `recovery-share-1:{did}` (else `SHARE_NOT_STORED` — the staging slot must not be destroyed while it is the seed's only home), then deletes the `ceremony-staging` slot (the seed's and Share 2's last local copy). The `did` is threaded from the ceremony result so the check reads the exact identity just created (mirrors the re-key epilogue's `confirm_rekey`). Idempotent; invoked by the frontend when the Shamir backup screen's confirmation completes
- `src/share_ceremony.rs` — client-side share generation module: `CeremonyShareSet` (recovery key did:key + the three base32 envelope strings + the Share 3 word phrase, all share material in `Zeroizing`), `load_or_create(handle, pds_url)` (reuse a valid staged set or generate + stage a fresh one; the staging record stores the three envelopes only — the seed is recomputed via `combine_envelopes(share1, share2)` on load), `clear_staging()` (idempotent teardown), `STAGING_ACCOUNT` (`"ceremony-staging"`). **Fail-closed staging contract:** only a genuinely absent slot, or one staged for different ceremony inputs (a new handle/PDS is the user's explicit abandonment of the old attempt), permits fresh generation; a present-but-unreadable/corrupt record errors with `StagingCorrupt` and preserves the slot — it may be the exact set a prior attempt already bound to a genesis op and escrowed, so overwriting it would permanently destroy the recovery seed
- `src/share_recovery.rs` — the "Recover existing identity" ceremony (10 Tauri IPC commands), the consuming inverse of `share_ceremony.rs`: `start_share_recovery(identifier)` (resolve handle/did:plc via plc.directory, then auto-load Share 1 from the resolved DID's per-DID slot `recovery-share-1:{did}`, falling back to the legacy global `recovery-share-1`, when it holds a valid v2 envelope), `add_recovery_share(share)` (base32 or word-phrase entry; SHARE_CHECKSUM, SHARE_SET_MISMATCH — with both set_ids — and DUPLICATE_SHARE are distinct, pre-combine errors), `remove_recovery_share(index)`, the escrow-assisted path client `initiate_escrow_release()` / `request_escrow_release(otp?)` (targets the account's own PDS endpoint from the authoritative DID state; OTP opens the release, OTP-less calls poll the pending window; the server's uniform 401 maps to RELEASE_UNAUTHORIZED), `verify_recovery_shares()` (combine → `derive_recovery_keypair` → compare against the **authoritative plc.directory audit log**, never a cached doc — mismatch is SHARES_DO_NOT_MATCH_IDENTITY, before anything signs), `recover_identity()` (fresh per-DID device key; the recovery key signs the rotation op installing it at `rotationKeys[0]`; talks ONLY to plc.directory — the fully-sovereign path makes zero PDS requests until re-escrow; idempotent on retry; durably stages the epilogue before returning), `run_recovery_epilogue(skip_escrow?)` (resumable: swap the new recovery key into `rotationKeys[1]` signed by the new device key → re-escrow the new Share 2 over a stored-or-fresh device-key sovereign session → rewrite the recovered DID's per-DID slot `recovery-share-1:{did}` with read-back verify; each step recorded in the durable `recovery-epilogue` Keychain record as it completes), `get_pending_recovery_epilogue()` (launch-time resume hook), `confirm_recovery_backup()` (teardown gate mirroring `confirm_share_backup`; destroys the epilogue record only after the NEW Share 1 is verified durable in the per-DID slot). Session state (`AppState.share_recovery_state`) is in-memory by design — the pre-anchor phase restarts from the entry screen; only the epilogue persists. `ShareRecoveryError` serializes as `{ code: "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE" }` with camelCase fields
- `src/lib.rs::{prepare_did_web_ceremony,complete_did_web_ceremony}` — did:web sibling ceremony: obtains the same device key and pending account's reserved repo key, lets the frontend compose/export the reviewed `did.json`, then submits it to `POST /v1/dids` only after it is externally resolvable. Completion persists the upgraded session and the server-returned Shamir Share 1 into the per-DID slot `recovery-share-1:{did}` (the same convention as the client-share and re-key paths); managed-hosting selection then opts the account into `/v1/did-web/hosting`.
